claims.text: The specified low-temperature ID-HVAF i7 configuration will enable deposition of an approximately 150 μm FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The specified process will preserve coating integrity while minimizing as-sprayed oxidation.
The proposed FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 5–30 μm.
The feedstock contains Al-rich and Cr-rich microsegregated regions.
The feedstock has a BCC random-solid-solution structure.
The medium air/fuel-pressure setting previously demonstrated optimal deposition performance.
The intervention will produce a highly dense coating with approximately 0.2% porosity.
The deposited coating will have a uniform elemental distribution.
The deposited coating will retain the BCC random-solid-solution structure.
An interdiffusion zone of approximately 3 μm will form.
High-temperature exposure will produce a thin, dense, continuous, predominantly Al2O3 thermally grown oxide.
Low-temperature ID-HVAF processing minimizes oxidation during deposition.
The dense coating microstructure restricts oxygen ingress.
During high-temperature exposure, aluminum diffuses outward and reacts with oxygen to form a protective alumina scale.
Sluggish diffusion intrinsic to the HEA limits internal oxidation and mixed-oxide formation and thereby controls TGO growth.
Relative to coatings produced from the 15–45 μm feedstock, the intervention will provide enhanced oxidation resistance and lower internal oxidation.
Relative to the baseline, the intervention will produce slower growth of a thin, continuous alumina TGO.
The low- and high-air/fuel-pressure HVAF-i7 baseline coatings had porosities of 0.8% and 1.8%, respectively.
The low- and high-air/fuel-pressure HVAF-i7 baseline variants had deposition efficiencies of 73% and 53%, respectively.
The absence of reactive elements creates a risk of TGO thickening and spallation under severe exposure conditions.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline uses 15–45 μm feedstock, but the proposed initial state uses 5–30 μm feedstock while the intervention is presented as a torch-configuration change. Thus the hypothesis embeds an additional feedstock-size intervention and does not isolate the claimed single intervention.

The exposure is described as isothermal, but the conditions also specify repeated approximately 5-minute air-cooling cycles, which interrupt strictly isothermal exposure unless their timing and purpose are separately defined.
